metadata.title: Hydrogen Radial Explorer — The Yukawa Button Does Nothing
metadata.purpose: Viz-riff critique of qm2-hydrogen-radial-explorer.html — encodings, controls, honesty; not the quantum mechanics

beats.narration_text: Kia ora. Liam — in for Bear. One Claude prompt: build me a hydrogen radial-density explorer. D3, live in the browser. We are not here to re-teach the quantum mechanics. We are here to judge whether this visualization earns the physics it promises.

props.command: Hey Claude, write me a visualization for hydrogen radial probability density — sweep n and ℓ.
output: ✓ D3 v7 from CDN — no build step

beats.new_visual_element: ClaudeComposerAsk cold open — hydrogen density prompt

beats.narration_text: The sim opens on n equals 2, ℓ equals 0. Red curve: radial probability density P of r, shaded below. A dashed vertical line marks the mean radius. Red dots on the baseline locate the radial nodes. A readout panel fires six live values in red: n, ℓ, energy in electron-volts, node count, mean radius, and peak count. Four controls: n and ℓ dropdowns, an overlay toggle, and a Yukawa-screening button.
beats.new_visual_element: SOURCE-CUT output.mp4 — baseline n=2 ℓ=0 state

beats.narration_text: Walk ℓ from zero to two at n equals 3. ℓ equals 0: three peaks, two radial nodes, energy minus 1.51 electron-volts. Advance to ℓ equals 1: one node gone, energy unchanged. Advance to ℓ equals 2: zero nodes, still minus 1.51. Enable the overlay: all three curves appear simultaneously, labelled with the shared energy. This is the Coulomb degeneracy, displayed as a graphic fact.
beats.new_visual_element: SOURCE-CUT change.mp4 — scripted n=3 ℓ sweep 0→1→2 then overlay

beats.narration_text: Three things earn this viz. The overlay is the argument: three orbital shapes, three different mean radii, one shared energy label — Coulomb degeneracy is visible before you write any algebra. The live readout names radial nodes as n minus ℓ minus one, which students can verify against the curve on every click. And the mean-radius line moves left as ℓ rises, showing that angular momentum trades radial extent for fewer oscillations — a spatial encoding that is true to the equation.
beats.new_visual_element: Freeze-frame change.mp4 t=11s — overlay active, all n=3 states with Coulomb degeneracy label

beats.narration_text: Three failures. First: the Yukawa-screening button does nothing. The code sets a flag that the update function never reads. Clicking it is instructively inert — physics implied, effect absent. Second: the x-axis domain is twenty n-squared Bohr radii, so for n equals 3 roughly eighty percent of the canvas is empty. Spatial comparison across n values is visually impossible. Third: both axes rescale on every ℓ change, erasing amplitude information. The ℓ-zero and ℓ-two peaks appear the same height — they are not; the y-axis was remapped.
beats.new_visual_element: Freeze-frame output.mp4 t=3s — n=2 ℓ=0 showing empty x-axis and Yukawa button

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. The overlay delivers Coulomb degeneracy as a visual argument. Best used after students have derived the wavefunction — the overlay confirms algebra, it does not replace it. But before this goes in front of a class: the Yukawa button must be removed or implemented. A control that promises to show how degeneracy breaks, and does nothing, damages the sim's credibility on everything else.

props.artifactHeading: Riff on the viz, not the physics
artifactLines: Overlay delivers Coulomb degeneracy — three shapes, one energy
Live readout checks radial-node arithmetic on every click
Mean-radius line encodes spatial contraction at constant energy
Yukawa screening button is wired to nothing
x-axis domain leaves 80% of canvas empty at n = 3
Verdict: use after deriving ψ_{nℓ} — fix or remove the Yukawa button first

beats.narration_text: Your turn. I have a D3 visualization of hydrogen radial probability density that lets users select n and ℓ. There is a Yukawa screening button that currently does nothing. I want you to implement it. Add a slider that sweeps a screening length λ from 1 to 20 Bohr radii. Use a fourth-order Runge-Kutta solver for the radial Schrödinger equation with the Yukawa potential V of r equals negative e-squared over r times exponential of negative r over λ. Show the modified P of r as a dashed overlay on top of the hydrogen curve. Update the energy readout to show the screened eigenvalue and the shift delta-E in electron-volts. Three concrete deliverables: implement the RK4 radial solver, add the screening slider, and show the energy shift in the readout panel.

props.command: I have a D3 viz of hydrogen radial probability density P(r)=r²|R_{nℓ}(r)|² with n and ℓ dropdowns. The Yukawa screening button does nothing. Implement it: add a slider for screening length λ (1–20 a₀), use RK4 to solve the radial Schrödinger equation with V(r) = −e²/(r·a₀)·exp(−r/λ), show the modified P(r) as a dashed overlay, and display ΔE in eV in the readout. Three deliverables: (1) RK4 radial solver, (2) λ slider with default λ=∞, (3) ΔE in the readout panel.
